# Operator guide {#sec-operator-guide}

This guide is for the operator who runs the development surface. The surface is
dev-only and ships in no release artefact.

## The visual workbench

The workbench applies a visual change at run time. It registers four actions
under the `AEE Dev` category in the CBA keybind menu.

| Action | What it does |
|---|---|
| `DevReapplyVisual` | Releases each effect scope and re-runs the visual pipeline, so a change is seen without a relaunch. |
| `DevScreenshot` | Takes a labelled screenshot and logs the paired AEE state line. |
| `DevDump` | Writes the full state dump. |
| `DevOverlayToggle` | Shows the state dump in an overlay. |

Bind each action in the CBA keybind menu under the `AEE Dev` category.

## The screenshot

The `DevScreenshot` action writes an image to the Arma profile `Screenshots`
folder. The file name is `aee_<label>_<timestamp>.png`. The paired state line in
the RPT names the file and the AEE state that produced it, so the image and the
state are captured together.

## The manual verdict

The visual check is manual. The engine renders on a client only, and a
dedicated server renders nothing. No automated gate reads a pixel, so the
rendered look is an operator-only observation.

The operator presses `DevReapplyVisual`, looks at the result, and confirms the
change. The `DevScreenshot` image is the evidence for that manual check. It is
not an automated gate, and no test asserts the image.
